nhtsa.note: NHTSA's complaint and recall model list only has the RX-7 for the 1993 model year, so 1994 and 1995 cars may show no data.

us.x: Sold new in the US for the 1993 to 1995 model years; fewer than 14,000 were sold here. Japanese-market FDs were built until 2002 and can be imported once they are 25 years old.

films.x: Dom drives a red 1993 RX-7 to the opening street race. The film used a privately owned car, repainted red so it would stand out.
Orange Julius races an orange RX-7. One of the first film's RX-7s was reused for it with a new body kit and graphics.

gens.tag: 1.3-liter twin-rotor 13B-REW, sequential twin turbos, 255 hp, 8,000 rpm redline.

variants.name: RX-7

trans.note: 4-speed automatic optional on base and Touring; limited-slip standard

variants.what: The no-frills version, still with the limited-slip differential; a 4-speed automatic was optional.

variants.name: RX-7 Touring
variants.what: Leather, a glass sunroof, fog lights, a rear wiper and the Bose Acoustic Wave stereo with CD player. The PEP package took its place for 1995.

variants.name: RX-7 R1 / R2
variants.what: R1 for 1993, R2 for 1994-95: stiffer springs, Bilstein shocks, a front strut brace, an extra oil cooler, a front lip and rear wing, and no cruise control.

13B-REW.name: Mazda 13B-REW
facts: 255 hp at 6,500 rpm, 217 lb-ft at 5,000 rpm (US)
Sequential: one turbo at low rpm, the second joins around 4,500 rpm; boost about 10 psi
Burns oil by design; PistonHeads says a quarter of a litre per 1,000 miles is normal

issues.rx: apex seals?|side seals?|low compression|compression test|engine rebuild
issues.x: PistonHeads says a compression test shows whether the apex and side seals are wearing out. Readings of 7 to 8 bar are good; lower is a concern, and a low reading means a rebuild is likely.
The sequential turbos are run by a rat's nest of 67 vacuum hoses, says Driving Line. Sports Car Market says engine heat made the hoses shrivel up and fail.
issues.fix: Replace the vacuum hoses with strong synthetic rubber ones.

issues.t: Coolant seals and air separator tank
issues.x: PistonHeads says steam from the exhaust at start-up points to coolant seals going brittle with age and heat. The air separator tank can split and leak coolant.
